description: This dataset gathers the map layers that the Global Logistics Cluster uses to support humanitarian supply operations in Ukraine since March 2022. It covers entry and exit points, ports, supply routes, roads, railways, reception points and roads in Poland, each offered as an ArcGIS Online feature service and as a GeoJSON extract on the Humanitarian Data Exchange. The Logistics Cluster, led by the World Food Programme, compiles the layers from direct observation and reports from partners, and points users to its LogIE platform for real-time downloads. The GeoJSON extracts are refreshed semi-manually when an automated process detects changes in the feature services. All layers are free to download or query without registration under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Coverage is Ukraine and the border crossings used to reach it. Caveats: status attributes change quickly in wartime, the extracts can lag the live services, and the metadata do not document attributes. Simulation uses: routes, border points and reception sites for relief supply chain and access models during conflict. Related records: the WFP SDI-T logistics database (data-wfp-logistics-database-sdi-t) holds global border crossings, bridges and obstacles from the same logistics community.
